description: Sensor/collector connectivity and configuration health for PCA: connected vs disconnected sensors across the data path (TC/agents -> Sensor Collector -> Fedex) and the config path (Sensor Collector -> Foxtrot, TC control channel), plus skylight-aaa certificate/auth health. Descriptions include what to check to fix a connectivity or configuration failure. Swarm: existing application metrics only.

options.content:
# PCA Sensor Connectivity & Configuration

Shows which sensors/collectors are **connected vs disconnected**, for both the **data path** and the **configuration path**, and surfaces the most common root causes (auth, certificates, reverse-proxy/network).

**Paths covered**
- **Sensor Agents → Sensor Collector (roadrunner)** — overall connectivity & health of ALL edge agents, measured with the common `roadrunner_agent_connected` signal (telemetry collectors register on the same data gateway under the same agentId, so they are included here, not treated as a separate group).
- **Telemetry Collector / File (NID) / MQTT detail (subsets)** — agent-type-specific metrics that add extra detail for the sensor agents that expose them (other agent types simply won't have these series, which is expected).
- **Sensor Collector → Fedex** (data) and **→ Foxtrot** (configuration)
- **skylight-aaa** certificate & authentication health

**Reverse proxy (nginx):** there is no nginx Prometheus exporter, so nginx is treated as part of a direct path – a proxy/network/DNS problem between a collector and PCA shows up as a `roadrunner_connection = 0`, websocket teardowns/rejections, or `roadrunner_foxtrot_connection_error` in the rows below.

**Filters:** `$tenant`, `$zone`, `$connectorId` are applied only where each metric carries that label. Each summary tile shows **up% + connected/total** so the denominator is always visible (e.g. '100% · 45 of 45'); 'n/a · total 0' means nothing of that type is monitored. Detailed per-entity red/green status is in the rows below.

**Swarm availability:** Uses existing application/exporter metrics only. Optional services and inactive data paths may have no data. Missing metrics are not evidence that a service is healthy; zero traffic can also be normal.

panels.description: Sensor Collectors connected to Fedex for data, shown as up% plus connected/total (roadrunner_connection). GREEN = all connected. ORANGE/RED = some/most not connected. 'n/a' with total 0 means nothing of this type is currently monitored (not an error). If connected < total, expand 'Sensor Collector → Fedex'.
panels.title: Collectors connected (data → Fedex)

panels.description: Sensor Collectors connected to Foxtrot for configuration, as up% plus connected/total (foxtrot_connector_connected). GREEN = all connected. ORANGE/RED = some/most not connected. 'n/a' with total 0 means nothing of this type is currently monitored (not an error). If connected < total, expand 'Sensor Collector → Foxtrot'.
panels.title: Collectors connected (→ Foxtrot)

panels.description: Sensor Collectors that successfully received configuration from Foxtrot, as up% plus configured/total (foxtrot_connector_configured). GREEN = all connected. ORANGE/RED = some/most not connected. 'n/a' with total 0 means nothing of this type is currently monitored (not an error). Configured < connected means connected-but-not-configured – check Foxtrot config/logs.
panels.title: Collectors configured

panels.description: Sensor agents connected to their Sensor Collector, as up% plus connected/total (roadrunner_agent_connected). GREEN = all connected. ORANGE/RED = some/most not connected. 'n/a' with total 0 means nothing of this type is currently monitored (not an error). If connected < total, expand 'Sensor Agents → Sensor Collector'.
panels.title: Sensor agents connected

panels.description: Client-certificate authorization requests rejected by skylight-aaa in the last hour. RED = sensors/collectors being refused at auth (often expired/revoked certs or tenant mismatch) – expand 'Certificates & Authentication'.
panels.title: Cert-auth rejections (1h)
Sensor Agents → Sensor Collector — Connectivity & Health (all agents)

panels.description: Per-agent connection state (1=connected) for EVERY sensor agent attached to the Sensor Collector – this includes telemetry collectors (they register on the same OpenMetrics data gateway, keyed on the same agentId). This is the common health signal for the whole Sensor Agent population. Red/0 or a dropped line = that agent stopped reporting to the collector; check the agent host, its network path, and its auth/cert.
panels.title: Sensor Agents – Connection Status (per agent)

panels.description: Number of sensor-agent connections the collector sees (data + admin) and duplicate connection requests. A sudden drop in connections = agents dropped off. Rising duplicates = agents reconnecting repeatedly (flapping). CHECK agent-side network stability and for duplicate agentIds / two agents sharing an identity.
panels.title: Sensor Agents – Connected Count & Duplicate Requests

panels.description: Data messages the collector dropped from agents, by cause. GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: any sustained rate → data loss at ingress even though the agent is connected. CHECK the cause label (e.g. buffer full, parse/validation).
panels.title: Sensor Agents – Dropped Data Messages (by cause)

panels.description: 1 = connected to the broker/Sensor Collector, 0 = disconnected. If 0 the TC cannot deliver data. CHECK: the TC process/pod is running; the network path from the TC site to the Sensor Collector endpoint (firewall / reverse proxy / DNS); and the data-channel authentication panel below. OPTIONAL stage – if no TC is deployed this is empty.
panels.title: Telemetry Collector – Data Channel Connection

panels.description: The management (control) channel carries configuration from the Sensor Orchestrator to the TC. 1 = connected, 0 = disconnected. If 0 the TC cannot receive config updates. CHECK: management endpoint reachability, the management-channel auth panel below, and the Sensor Orchestrator. NOTE: sensor-orchestrate exposes no Prometheus metrics, so this relayed channel status is the available config-reachability signal for TCs.
panels.title: Telemetry Collector – Control / Config Channel Connection

panels.description: Authentication outcomes on the TC data and management channels. Rising authenticationError/Failure with little/no Successful = the TC is being rejected. CHECK: the TC client certificate validity/expiry (Certificates row), tenant/credential config, and the skylight-aaa cert-auth rejection panel.
panels.title: Telemetry Collector – Authentication (data + control)

panels.description: Batches queued inside the TC because it cannot ship to the Sensor Collector. GOOD: low/stable. BAD: steadily growing → the data channel is down or the collector is not accepting. CHECK the data-channel connection above and the 'Sensor Collector → Fedex' row.
panels.title: Telemetry Collector – Outbound Backlog (batchesInQueue)
Sensor Agents → File / NID source detail (subset)

panels.description: NID devices deliver data by writing files to a directory that the Sensor Collector's filewatcher consumes (an alternative to streaming agents). 'in watched dir' = files currently present; 'enqueued' = files picked up and waiting to be processed. GOOD: both stay low/stable (files consumed as fast as they arrive). BAD: 'in watched dir' grows unbounded = the collector is not consuming (filewatcher stuck / roadrunner down); both flat at 0 when you expect data = the NID devices are not writing. CHECK: the NID device is exporting files; the shared location/mount is reachable, writable and not full; and the roadrunner/sensor-collector process and its filewatcher are running.
panels.title: File Sources (NID) – Files In Watched Directory & Enqueued

panels.description: Problems the filewatcher hit processing NID files. failed = files it could not process (bad format/content); requeued = files picked up before being fully written (writer/timing issue); nack = negative acks with a reason. GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: failed/nack rising = malformed files or incomplete writes, so data from those NID files is lost. CHECK: the file format matches the configured parser; the NID writes atomically (write to a temp name then rename) so the watcher never sees a partial file; and the nack reason label.
panels.title: File Sources (NID) – File Processing Issues

panels.description: Average time the collector spends reading a raw file from disk, parsing it, and normalizing it per GetData cycle. GOOD: low/stable. BAD: rising read time = slow disk/mount to the NID file location; rising parse/normalize = large or complex files. Sustained increases precede a growing 'in watched dir' backlog above.
panels.title: File Sources (NID) – Read / Parse / Normalize Time

panels.description: For sources that feed the collector over MQTT. GOOD: successfully_consumed > 0, errors flat. BAD: connection_error > 0 or not_consumed rising with no successful → the MQTT source is not delivering. CHECK the MQTT broker reachability and the source device.
panels.title: Other Sources – MQTT Connectivity

panels.description: Each Sensor Collector's data connection to PCA (Fedex). 1 = connected, 0 = disconnected. 0 = that collector cannot deliver data and it backs up in its local persistence cache. Because this path traverses the reverse proxy, a 0 can also mean a proxy / network / DNS problem between the collector and PCA. CHECK: collector running; outbound reachability to the PCA data endpoint; the websocket and rejected-batch panels; and certificate validity (Certificates row).
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Data Connection to Fedex

panels.description: Fedex-side websocket closes (teardown) and refused connection attempts (rejected, with reason). GOOD: flat. BAD: repeated for a connector → it cannot hold a connection. CHECK the reason label; the usual causes are auth/cert failures (Certificates row) and tenant mismatches (next panel).
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Websocket Teardowns / Rejections

panels.description: Batches Fedex rejected: unauthorized tenant (the collector's tenantId does not match its authorized websocket – a provisioning/config issue), bad data (unparseable), or internal error. GOOD: flat at 0. CHECK provisioning/tenant config for unauthorized; collector data quality for bad_data; Fedex logs for internal.
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Rejected Batches (by cause)

panels.description: Time for the collector to ship a batch to Fedex and receive an ack (roadrunner_data_ship_latency_ms). GOOD: low/stable. BAD: rising → a degraded (not yet down) link – proxy/network latency or Fedex under load. Sustained high latency typically precedes disconnects.
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Data Ship Latency

panels.description: Data the Sensor Collector (roadrunner) has buffered to its on-disk persistence cache because it has not yet shipped to Fedex (roadrunner_persistence_service_cached_files = data files, _available_batches = batches ready to ship), per collector. This is the direct symptom of a data-path problem: when the 'Data Connection to Fedex' above drops or the link degrades, data accumulates here. GOOD: flat/near zero. BAD: steadily rising → the collector cannot deliver to Fedex – check the connection, websocket teardown and rejected-batch panels above; a persistently growing cache risks filling the collector's disk and dropping data.
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Persistence Cache Backlog (unshipped to Fedex)

panels.description: Foxtrot's view of each connector's control connection (foxtrot_connector_connected). 1 = connected, 0 = disconnected. 0 = the collector cannot reach Foxtrot for configuration, even if its data path to Fedex is healthy. CHECK: outbound reachability to the Foxtrot/config endpoint through the proxy; certificate/auth; and the collector-side Foxtrot error panel below.
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Connection to Foxtrot

panels.description: 1 = the connector successfully requested and received its configuration from Foxtrot; 0 = connected but not (yet) configured or the config push failed. If connected (above) but not configured: CHECK Foxtrot logs and the config-request error panel below, and verify a valid connector config exists for this tenant/zone.
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Configured by Foxtrot

panels.description: Errors the collector itself reports connecting to Foxtrot (roadrunner_foxtrot_connection_error) and retrieving/parsing configuration (roadrunner_configuration_error). GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: >0 → the collector is failing to reach Foxtrot or process its config. CHECK the network path to Foxtrot and the config content/validity.
panels.title: Sensor Collector – Foxtrot / Config Errors (collector-side)

panels.description: Config/control messages Foxtrot handled, grouped by resulting HTTP code, plus unhandled messages. GOOD: 2xx only. BAD: a rise in 4xx/5xx or unhandled → Foxtrot is receiving requests but failing them. CHECK Foxtrot logs for the failing message type and code.
panels.title: Foxtrot – Config Request Handling (by HTTP code)

panels.description: Client-certificate authorization requests skylight-aaa rejected, by reason. GOOD: flat at 0. BAD: >0 → sensors/collectors are being refused at authentication – this is frequently the root cause of the websocket rejections in the Fedex row. Common reasons: expired/revoked certificate, unknown CA, tenant mismatch.
panels.title: Cert Authorization Rejections (skylight-aaa, by reason)

panels.description: Outcome of OCSP revocation checks for client certificates. GOOD: only 'good'. BAD: any 'revoked'/'unknown' → the affected sensors will be refused at connection. CHECK whether the certificate was intentionally revoked; reissue/rotate if the revocation is unexpected.
panels.title: Client Certificate OCSP Status

panels.description: Days until each Sensor Collector's client certificate expires (derived from roadrunner_cert_expiry). An expired cert = immediate auth failure and disconnect. GOOD: comfortably above 30d (green). WARN < 30d (orange), CRITICAL < 14d (red). Renew/rotate the collector certificate before it reaches 0.
panels.title: Sensor Collector Client Cert – Days to Expiry

panels.description: Days until each tenant's intermediate CA certificate expires (skylight_aaa_tenant_cert_expiry_days). Expiry here affects ALL of that tenant's sensors at once. GOOD: > 30d (green). WARN < 30d, CRITICAL < 14d → rotate the tenant CA well before expiry.
panels.title: Tenant CA Certificate – Days to Expiry

panels.description: Per-tenant counts of active vs revoked client certificates (skylight_aaa_client_certificates_active / _revoked). A rising revoked count or a drop in active = certificates being revoked/removed, which will disconnect those sensors. CHECK why certs are being revoked (rotation, decommission, or compromise).
panels.title: Client Certificates – Active vs Revoked

title: PCA Sensor Connectivity & Configuration
